"Satisfy is a full-dive VRMMO developed by the S.A. Group and regulated by the supercomputer Morpheus. It has a player base exceeding 2 billion, runs on ultra-realistic AI for NPCs (making them nearly indistinguishable from players except by green name tags for ordinary NPCs), and emphasizes player-driven world development with minimal developer intervention. Time flows at a 3:1 ratio (1 real-world hour ≈ 3 in-game hours). Sessions last up to 20 hours, after which players are forced offline for 6 hours. There is no customer service center; the world evolves through player actions, NPC interactions, and information exchange.⁠Overgeared.fandom

The world is vast (West Continent alone larger than Earth), with continents, seas, kingdoms, empires, dungeons, fields, and later divine/mythic dimensions. Players log in via capsules. Character creation has limited customization (appearance close to real life with options for skin, hair, eyes, tattoos, weight, but height/skeletal structure largely fixed). Originally human-only; non-human races require hidden quests or special conditions.⁠Overgeared.fandom

Core Mechanics
Death and penalties: Beginners under level 10 lose no experience on death (quest failure still penalizes). Dying twice within 24 hours locks the account for 12 hours. Timed quests cannot be safely exited. Killed entities fade into grey light.
Stun: Taking ≥40% health in one hit stuns the character.
Weight and inventory: Exceeding weight limit slows movement proportionally (e.g., 200% excess halves speed and risks “weakened” state). Warehouses exist in communities (registration + password; summonable via magic; small fees to open/store).
Travel: Walking, mounts, carriages (base 5 gold in safe zones; higher in dangerous areas for risk), and later teleportation or dimensional travel. Carriages help cross monster areas safely.
Parties: Up to 24 members (players or NPCs). Leader sets loot rules (e.g., leader distribution, need/greed). Shared affinity changes and some buffs. Useful for raids and hunting.
Currency: Gold, silver, bronze (roughly 1 gold = 100 silver). Auction house commissions scale with item rating (higher for rarer items). Real-money conversion exists and is significant (e.g., early values around 100 gold ≈ substantial real currency).
Control and movement: Full-body realism. Characters respond to player intent like a real body, modified by system correction, stats, terrain, and skills. “Control” refers to skillful prediction, positioning, timing, weak-point targeting, evasion of non-targeted attacks, blocking, countering, and efficient skill use. Terrain matters (e.g., heavy boots in desert sink into sand). Combat is action-oriented rather than pure tab-targeting.
Stats: Core stats include Strength (attack power, health, weight limit; effects awaken/improve every 100 levels), Stamina, Agility, Intelligence (magic power/mana), plus class-specific ones like Dexterity (production). Players get 10 fixed stat points per level; NPCs get variable (6–20). Named NPCs have superior base capabilities and much higher effective health.
Classes: Over 120,000 possible. Ratings: Normal (common, white font), Rare, Epic, Unique, Legendary, Myth (and growth types or “Only One”). Hidden classes (Rare+) are special. Types: combat (easy leveling via monsters), production (raise stats via crafting/selling; often have Dexterity), and others. Advancements every 100 levels unlock more skills/potential. Legendary classes (very few) grant major privileges like wearing restricted gear (with penalties until understanding is gained) and control immunity.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Items and ratings: Same rating scale (Normal → Myth). Equipment has slots, visible appearance, durability (needs repair), and usage conditions (level/stats/class—Legendary classes often ignore these with penalties). Enhancement up to +10 using stones; success chance drops with higher enhancement and rating. Success = +1; failure = –3. Higher enhancements add auras/lights (blue at +6, deeper colors later, white at +9). Options, creator signatures (especially high-grade), and understanding systems exist. Production methods, blueprints, and materials heavily influence outcome.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Other systems: Quests (ratings, timed, failure penalties), titles, skills (with cooldowns, grades), pets (taming expanded later), affinity with NPCs (shared in parties; high affinity unlocks stories/growth), reputation. Later “First Update” added Spiritual Energy/cultivation ranks, Treasures (no usage restrictions but resource costs; risky crafting), expanded pet taming, etc.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Crafting / Production Systems
Production classes (especially blacksmiths) are central. Most blacksmiths use an automated system: select design/production method, register materials, start process (hammering auto-runs; 5 min–several hours). Better materials raise rating chances. Manual labor (physically hammering) increases odds of higher ratings and options and is favored by rankers.⁠Novgo

Factors affecting quality: skill level, materials, time, tools (hammers with bonuses), dexterity, understanding of items (disassemble/repair/use to raise understanding → eventually learn recipes and reduce equip penalties), and special skills. Legendary blacksmithing (e.g., Pagma’s Successor path) masters basic skills, opens advanced ones (creation, appraisal, repair, disassemble, etc.), allows designing new production methods, raises chances for Rare/Epic/Unique/Legendary outputs, permanently boosts stats/reputation on high-tier crafts, and lets the creator’s name appear on items. High-grade crafted gear can have extended safe enhancement ranges or signature prestige.⁠Anilore

Smithies/forges are workplaces. Minerals, ores, special materials (scales, metals from specific regions/dimensions), and later Treasures expand options. Crafting drives economy, player reputation, guild power, and plot—high-end gear is social and political currency.

The World and Places
West Continent is the primary starting area: massive, populated by billions, home to numerous kingdoms and the former Saharan Empire (later integrated into the Overgeared Empire). Separated from the East Continent by the Red Sea. Diverse climates—northern cold/snowfields, deserts, mountains, forests, canyons, swamps, plains.⁠Overgeared.fandom

Key locations (vividly):

Reinhardt: Former capital of Eternal Kingdom, later capital of Overgeared Kingdom/Empire. Bustling political, military, and industrial hub with temples, smithies, academies, fortifications, and expanding infrastructure. Grows into a center of power with divine elements later.
Winston: Large northern city, early hub for Grid. Home to Khan’s famous smithy. Busy streets, commercial districts, noble presence (Steim family influence), and surrounding threats from churches or monsters.
Reidan: Once a declining desert/arid territory granted as a duchy. Harsh sands, limited water, sparse population initially. Transformed into an industrial powerhouse and supply center through farming innovations, mining, and development. Features mountains (Dravian), fields, and strategic value.
Bairan: Smaller village near Winston that becomes a guild base. More rural, with smithing and adventuring opportunities.
Patrian: Major fortress city, militaristic atmosphere, frequent early player activity.
Titan: Former Saharan capital, chosen for its unique black mithril mine. Imperial grandeur—palaces, legions, economic power.
Galest: Largest port city of the former empire, gateway to the Red Sea, economic artery with ships, trade, and coastal vibrancy.
Other notable areas: Kesan Canyon (steep, dangerous walls; hermit hideouts), Dravian Mountains (former dragon nest, monster-infested), northern snowfields (Frost Orcs, harsh cold), Cokro Island Dungeon (multi-floor with periodic boss Hell Gao), various temples (Yatan Church sites of dark rituals, Rebecca Church holy sites), fields/plains for hunting, and later Overgeared World (mythic divine dimension tied to gods and temples in Reinhardt, granting special effects).
East Continent features different kingdoms (Hwan, Cho, Kaya, etc.) with distinct cultures, martial/spiritual elements, and access challenges. Hell, divine realms, Abyss (between dimensions/servers), and other planes appear later. Servers function as “dimensions” with unique resources, bosses, and travel costs/limits via the Abyss.⁠Invenglobal

Kingdoms/Empires include Eternal (northern, later conquered), Saharan (vast imperial power with Red Knights, later declined/integrated), Gauss, Fold, Siren (aquatic elements), Valhalla, and many others (some destroyed or vassalized). Politics involve nobility, churches (Rebecca vs. Yatan), guilds, and player kingdoms.

Major NPCs
There are thousands of NPCs; exhaustive coverage of every minor one is impossible. Named/super-named NPCs have gold names, infinite growth potential, high health, story impact, and superior capabilities. Semi-named can break limits with training. Ordinary NPCs have green names and stat caps. High affinity unlocks depth, quests, and growth. Treating them as real people yields strong results.⁠Overgeared.fandom

Key named NPCs (descriptions based on established lore):

Khan: Elderly, pot-bellied blacksmith craftsman of Winston, descendant of Albatino (first human craftsman). Proud family tradition of excellence. Firm-willed, initially pressured by corrupt companies. Becomes Grid’s teacher, friend, and father figure; later Chief of Reinhardt’s smithy and rises to Legendary Blacksmith. Completes masterwork pieces even near death. Deep loyalty and insight.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Irene (Irene Winston von Steim): Beautiful noblewoman with silver hair, clear blue eyes, and elegant oval face. Only daughter/successor of Earl (later Duke) Steim. Kidnapped by Yatan Church and rescued; later marries Grid, becomes lady of Winston, queen/empress figure. Dutiful, status-aware but not arrogant; develops cooking/baking hobbies to please Grid. Loyal knights; mother to Lord.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Piaro: Former Captain of Saharan Empire’s Red Knights, Legendary Farmer, and Great Swordsman. Initially a ragged, matted-haired hermit in Kesan Canyon seeking revenge (sickness of the heart). Becomes Grid’s duke, general, and agricultural backbone. Wears straw hat and farming tools; turns farming tools and everyday objects into devastating weapons via qi. Married to elf Beniyaru; has daughter. Loyal, grows into a mythic-tinged powerhouse.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Braham (Braham Eshwald): Direct descendant vampire (child of Beriache), Legendary Great Magician, Duke of Wisdom. Transcendently beautiful—pale skin, blood-red eyes, sharp fangs; appearance causes strong reactions. Arrogant, views most as fools, pursues ultimate knowledge/magic. Complex history of experiments, regrets (Mumud), grudges (Pagma, Marie Rose). High affinity leads to deep alliance with Grid; later divine aspects.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Asmophel: Former Red Knight colleague of Piaro. Complex past involving brainwashing/drugs and crimes; seeks atonement. Loyal subordinate and commander under Grid; skilled knight.
Mercedes: Legendary Knight, top Saharan talent, later high-ranking Overgeared figure (commander). Extremely capable in combat and negotiations.
Lord Steim: Son of Grid and Irene; prodigious young noble with strong potential and protection details.
Jude: Semi-named/Grade A knight under Grid; high combat stats, loyal, grows significantly.
Minor: Semi-named miner/metals detector; unique skills, breaks limits through development.
Rabbit: Administrator/merchant type; economic expertise for the kingdom.
Kasim: Assassin (later Lantier path); protects Lord and leads shadows.
Sticks: Elven Great Sage; knowledge and support.
Others of note: Earl/Marquis Ashur (powerful magician, complex relations), Bland (magic swordsman turned farmer enthusiast), Smith (blacksmith who grows under Grid’s influence), various blacksmiths (White, Enoch, etc.), church figures (Isabel of Rebecca), emperors/princes of Saharan (Juander, etc.), and many more (Noll the vampire, Ke’ong the dwarf, etc.). Super-named include legends and major world influencers.
NPCs drive stories, provide quests, grow with or against players, and form the living backbone of the world. Affinity, training, and genuine interaction are key to unlocking their full potential.

This captures the core systems, geography, and prominent NPCs of Satisfy’s worldview as detailed across the novel, wiki, and related sources. The setting prioritizes realism, player agency, crafting depth, and emergent politics over pure combat progression.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game inspired by the Satisfy/Overgeared setting, or adapt an existing game.
- Deliver the game without clarifying questions, making reasonable assumptions.

## Requirements
- Implement a playable game now; briefly note assumptions when finishing.
- Include player-driven world development, action combat, crafting, quests, NPC interaction, progression, and realistic world details.

## Decisions
- No existing game was present, so work proceeded as a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript game.
- The game is a top-down Winston adventure with slime combat, Khan quests and smithing, inventory, XP/leveling, health tonics, and local saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game interface, canvas world, HUD, start screen, dialogs, inventory, desktop controls, and mobile controls.
- Added game state, world rendering, movement, slime combat, leveling, HUD updates, quest/dialog interactions, crafting, and local save state.
- Loaded scripts in dependency order: `game.js`, `game-world.js`, `game-loop.js`, `game-ui.js`.
- Rebuilt `style.css` with desktop and mobile layouts; JavaScript syntax checks passed.
- Captured desktop and mobile screenshots; the start screen and game scene render without reported page errors.

### Active
- Verify the full play flow in-browser, including starting, interacting with Khan, accepting/completing the quest, crafting, combat, and inventory.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Capture the started game and check for runtime errors using `CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR='#enterButton'` with the capture script.
2. Exercise the quest, combat, crafting, and inventory flows; fix any issues found.
3. Summarize the finished game and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and script load order.
- `game.js`: Core state, save data, canvas, and terrain.
- `game-world.js`: World, NPC, enemy, and player rendering.
- `game-loop.js`: HUD updates, movement, combat, and leveling.
- `game-ui.js`: Khan dialogs, quest and crafting actions, controls, and inventory behavior.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- Earlier `ReferenceError: $ is not defined` stemmed from incomplete script loading; script tags have since been added in dependency order.
- The capture helper did not auto-start because “ENTER THE WORLD” does not match its default start-button label filter; use the explicit selector `#enterButton`.
- Planned quest: defeat three slimes, then return to Khan for 80 XP and 12 gold; crafting a Fieldsteel Blade costs 2 Iron Ore and 20 gold.
- Changes are uncommitted.
